files.workflow_packages/product.analytics_brie: Read inputs and apply the analytics-brief skill. Write only reports/PRODUCT_ANALYTICS.md.

---
name: analytics-brief
description: Compile a bounded evidence-based analytics brief.
---

Create a standing product analytics brief for any project with its own PostHog connection. A saved configuration captures the PostHog project, exclusions, reporting window and cadence. Inspect event definitions and semantics before analysis. Produce five sections: activation using ordered funnels, key-event trends, traffic or an explicit unavailable finding, error signals, and one justified breakdown or insufficient-evidence finding. Every table states window, population, exclusions and whether it counts events, people or organizations. Use SQL/Python to verify arithmetic and ordered progression. Never infer ordered conversion from unrelated event totals. Include reproducible queries and evidence references, disclose instrumentation gaps and small samples, and give findings without recommendations. Credentials stay in Tin; query permissions must be read-only at the provider. Use aggregate output. Never join unrelated PostHog projects without a shared identity.

Setup: bind custom.api.posthog to the correct regional origin. A PostHog read-only key needs query and event-definition access. Enable POST only for query requests; gateway http.write is a transport capability, not provider permission to mutate data. Use request_service with alias analytics and stable step IDs. Inspect definitions with GET, query with POST. Stay within eight calls and bounded responses; aggregate in SQL. Reuse results locally with Python for checks. Do not retry an uncertain request under a new step ID. Failed auth or incomplete data must be reported, never invented. Use headings Activation, Key-event trends, Traffic, Error signals, Breakdown. Each can explicitly state unavailable. Verify dates and range. Fixed dates remain fixed on scheduled runs; rolling windows require a later input-contract revision. Report exact effective dates and exclusions. Query text and aggregate provenance belong in the report; omit individual identities.

Start the report with Status: complete or Status: incomplete. A failed required funnel query is incomplete, never zero. For valid ordered evidence, include Ordered funnel (projects): followed by the three verified counts separated by ->. The controlled qualification fixture has known answers; do not hardcode them in runtime calculations.

assumptions: Synthetic contract fixture; no provider access or real quality evaluation has occurred.
Fixed dates: a rolling window remains a required follow-up before recurring publication.
Controlled fixture: the three ordered project stages have 12, 7 and 3 distinct actors. These are synthetic expected values, not live measurements.
cost_drivers: Event discovery and query refinement consume agent calls; at most eight provider requests.
effects: Read-only analytics queries and one project report; the key must restrict provider-side writes.

cases.description: A controlled provider fixture with known ordered project counts; required-query failure is not an ordinary pass.

rubric.question: Do all figures match the cited queries, with ordered progression and explicit units?
Are unavailable or insufficient-evidence sections explicit rather than invented?
Has the exact emitted provider query been separately checked in its own dialect, including missing stages and empty results, rather than only translated to a local reference?

limitations: Synthetic output for testing the authoring pipeline, not a qualified analytics workflow.
Live permission checks, quality evaluation, rolling windows and bound calibration remain required.
